subject: Distributor fee allocation and audit onboarding
messages:
From: Sarah Evans <sarah.evans@cloudbarn.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cloudbarn.com, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@resellerco.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Distributor fee allocation and audit onboarding

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — CloudBarn is excited about the potential to list Redwood models in our marketplace. Before we move to final commercials, procurement has a couple of items they need clarified in the partner paper / addendum:

- Pass-through fee mechanics: do you expect CloudBarn to bill customers directly and remit a net amount to Redwood, or should Redwood invoice CloudBarn for gross usage?
- Audit scope: procurement wants the ability to audit a subset of transactions for a 24-month lookback. Would Redwood accept access to invoice-level records and an annual audit right?
- Liability carveouts: our legal team would like clarifying language around pass-through tax withholding and VAT handling.

I've attached an updated SOW and the reseller billing spreadsheet for reference (CloudBarn_SOW_v3.pdf). Can you confirm Redwood's preferred model and any constraints we should bake into the addendum?

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Evans
Head of Marketplace Operations
CloudBarn

[attachment: CloudBarn_SOW_v3.pdf (PDF, 482 KB)]

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Evans <sarah.evans@cloudbarn.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Distributor fee allocation and audit onboarding

Hi Sarah — great questions, thanks for outlining them. High level: Redwood prefers a net remittance model (CloudBarn bills end-customers, remits net to Redwood) for marketplace convenience, but we can be flexible depending on procurement / tax constraints.

Answers inline:
- Pass-through mechanics: net remittance is standard for our marketplace listings. We can add language requiring CloudBarn to provide monthly remittance statements and per-invoice detail in a structured CSV.
- Audit scope: an annual audit right limited to a calendar/fiscal year and scoped to a statistically reasonable sample is acceptable. We prefer no more than one third-party audit per 12 months and that Redwood be given notice and reasonable time to remediate findings.
- VAT/withholding: we typically require that marketplace platforms handle VAT and remit to local authorities; Redwood will accept documentation of tax withholdings and allow a gross-to-net reconciliation.

I'm attaching a starter addendum with our suggested language (Redwood_marketplace_addendum_draft.docx). Can your legal team mark up and we'll triage any deal blockers? We'd like to finalize language before the commercial signature next week.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick read below; attaching tracked changes (legal_comments_track_changes.docx). Key points: 

1) Audit scope: agree to annual audits but limit to a 12-month rolling window and allow Redwood to object to any third-party auditor for conflicts. Add language: "Audit scope shall be limited to transactions related to amounts remitted to Redwood under this Addendum for the immediately preceding twelve (12) month period."

2) Sampling & frequency: specify statistical sampling and cap audits at once per 12-month period unless systemic misrepresentation is discovered. Require a remediation period of 60 days before dispute escalation.

3) Pass-through liability: redact open-ended indemnities. Propose: "CloudBarn shall remit amounts collected less any taxes withheld under applicable law. Redwood's liability for fee adjustments shall be limited to amounts actually invoiced and remitted under this Addendum."

4) VAT & withholding: require CloudBarn to provide withholding certificates and allow gross-to-net reconciliation but not unilateral netting beyond documented withholdings.

5) Confidentiality & data access: narrow audit to invoice-level transaction IDs and summary IO fields; avoid providing customer PII. Require a DPA addendum or use secure transfer via SFTP for records.

I flagged proposed redlines in the doc; most are standard. If Ben thinks commercial needs a concession on audit frequency, we can consider an elevated SLA credit in lieu of audit rights.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwood.com <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Distributor fee allocation and audit onboarding — quick commercial input

Short note from a commercial POV:
- We should hold firm on limiting audit scope and capping frequency. Marketplace partners sometimes request broad audits when disputes arise — that kills time.
- For payflow, ask CloudBarn to remit net monthly and include a 30-day payment term.
- If procurement insists on a wider audit, offer a single right to expand scope in exchange for a 2% revenue credit for the prior 12 months (to move the deal).

Happy to jump on a 15-min call with CloudBarn to iron out the last mile.

Ben Carter
Head of Partnerships, Americas
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Evans <sarah.evans@cloudbarn.com>

Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Distributor fee allocation and audit onboarding

Karthik — thanks for the fast turnaround and Kimberly / Ben for inputs. CloudBarn is broadly comfortable with Redwood's proposed language with two asks:

1) Procurement would like audit lookback to be 24 months instead of 12; if Redwood cannot accept that, we can take your 12-month limit in exchange for a one-time reconciliation audit covering months 13–24 (no continuous rights).
2) For VAT/withholding we will provide certificates and agree to secure transfer for any PII-free reports.

Next steps: I'll upload our markups by EOD and kick a DocuSign envelope for the final addendum. Please confirm who should be the signer on Redwood's side (commercial or legal).

Best,
Sarah
